verdict.line: You lose extended trades from level 3 through the low-8s when Fiora chains Lunge into Burst of Speed, but you win the game once your Shadowflame/Rabadon's spike and R (Needlework) outrange her.

brief.thesis: Fiora's Q (Lunge) closes 600 range in an instant and can be thrown twice within a couple seconds for free, which beats Gwen's 450-range Q (Snip Snip!) in any straight skirmish. Her W (Riposte) also punishes a single overcommitted auto or dash, so Gwen has to poke from outside Lunge range and never feed her a free parry. That structural range/tempo gap is why this sits at 47.1% over 448 games even though Gwen is a coinflip 50.6% champion overall.

theirWindow.when: her Q and E are both up
theirWindow.what: Fiora chains Lunge into Burst of Speed, and every landed attack or Lunge during that window stacks extra move speed onto her — don't trade back into this, just disengage and let the wave crash.

yourWindow.what: Her parry threat is gone, so commit Skip 'n Slash (E) to dash in and auto freely — a landed hit during E's attack-speed window partially refunds the ability's own cooldown.

powerCurve.note: Both kits are thin; bait Riposte with a single auto
Lunge into Burst of Speed out-trades your 450-range Q
Blade Waltz (R) online, solo-kill threat is real
Skip 'n Slash cooldown falls, passive sustain catches up
Shadowflame/Rabadon's and Needlework range take over

start.item: Doran's Ring, Health Potion, Health Potion
start.why: 49.2% win rate over 465 games and the 85.5% pick — the extra potion charge matters because Fiora's Duelist passive heals her back on every hit she lands, so you need to out-sustain the early pokes, not just trade evenly.

boots.why: 51.9% win rate over 258 games and 52.4% pick — flat auto-attack reduction directly counters the extra attack speed Fiora gets from Burst of Speed (E) and the AD bump from activating Riposte (W).

core.why: First item in the 60%-win-rate, 65-game path — builds toward the mid-game spike you need to survive the levels 3-8 disadvantage window.
Second item in that same path — the magic pen and burst on low-health targets pairs directly with A Thousand Cuts' bonus damage as Fiora's health drops.
Closes out the 60% win-rate core — this is the item that flips the matchup once it's online, since your flat magic damage finally outscales her physical damage.

situational.when: you're ahead and want raw magic penetration over the auto-attack mitigation of Steelcaps
the game runs long and you need omnivamp to directly answer her Duelist passive healing
you're snowballing and want a burst-reset proc for repeated skirmishes

runes.keystoneWhy: Conqueror ramps through the short trades this lane forces on you — every Q snip and auto you land stacking it back while you're forced to poke rather than commit to a full combo.

summoners.why: 50% win rate and the clear 64.8% pick — Ignite matters specifically here because Fiora's Duelist passive heals her back through extended trades, and burning that sustain is what actually lets you close kills you start.

playing.title: Poke with Q, don't chase
playing.detail: Snip Snip! lands true damage in its center and triggers your passive on every snip out to 450 range — use it to chip her from outside her 600-range Lunge rather than stepping in to auto.

playing.title: Bait Riposte before committing
playing.detail: Riposte's cooldown is only 10-6s across ranks, so throw a single spare auto or Q snip to bait the parry before you dash in with E — eating a Riposte on your real engage wastes the whole trade.

playing.title: Hold W for her all-in
playing.detail: Hallowed Mist has a long 22-18s cooldown, so save it for the moment she commits Lunge into Burst of Speed — once you're in the mist she can only hit you by walking in, which kills her attack-speed window.

playing.title: Respect the double Lunge
playing.detail: Fiora can dash a second time within a couple seconds at no extra cost, so a single dodged Lunge does not mean you're safe — wait out the follow-up before you reset your own spacing.

playing.title: Play passive levels 6-8
playing.detail: Blade Waltz comes online at 6 and gives her a real all-in threat on top of her existing lane edge — avoid extended trades in this window and let minion waves do the work instead.

playing.title: Punish dead cooldowns with E
playing.detail: Once you see her Lunge or Riposte go down, dash in with Skip 'n Slash for the attack speed, range, and magic damage on-hit — landing a hit during that window partially refunds E itself.

playing.title: Scale into Needlework range
playing.detail: From the mid-teens on, your item spike and R's 1200 range let you poke and threaten from far outside anything in her kit — stop looking for skirmishes and start looking for Needlework picks.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and every win-rate figure above are measured from live games on the current patch (16.18.1); the trade-pattern and timing reasoning connecting them is my own read of the kits, not sourced data.
